care_scenario: The member has met the $1,000 deductible and has accumulated $2,800 toward the $3,000 out-of-pocket maximum. The member then receives a covered in-network service with an allowed amount of $1,000. No copayment or other charge applies.
cost_question: How much of the service's allowed amount will the member owe, and how much will the plan pay after applying the out-of-pocket maximum?
answer: The member will owe $200, reaching the $3,000 out-of-pocket maximum. The plan will pay $800 for the service, and nothing will remain before the member reaches the maximum.
reasoning: 1. The deductible is already met, so the $1,000 allowed amount is initially subject to 30% coinsurance, or $300. 2. The member is only $200 below the $3,000 out-of-pocket maximum ($3,000 - $2,800). 3. The member therefore pays only $200 of the otherwise applicable $300 coinsurance; after the maximum is reached, the plan pays the remainder of the covered allowed amount. 4. The plan pays $1,000 - $200 = $800, and the remaining out-of-pocket maximum is $0.
plan_document: For covered in-network services, the individual deductible is $1,000. After the deductible is met, the member pays 30% coinsurance and the plan pays 70% of the allowed amount. The $3,000 individual out-of-pocket maximum includes deductible payments and coinsurance. After the member reaches that maximum, the plan pays 100% of covered in-network allowed amounts for the rest of the plan year.

cost_breakdown.cost_sharing_method: Apply 30% coinsurance, limited to the $200 remaining before the out-of-pocket maximum; the plan pays the rest after the maximum is reached.
